title: Only 7% Can Name All These Hospital Items
summary: Beds, diagnostic tools and specialist hospital equipment become harder to identify across ten fast pictures.

landing.intro: From everyday ward essentials to specialist machines, see how many of these 10 hospital items you can name.

about.body:
This quick worldwide-English picture quiz presents ten pieces of hospital equipment, ranging from familiar ward items to diagnostic and sterilisation devices. Every question asks you to recognise the object shown rather than recall a medical procedure or local healthcare policy.

The photographs are used with permission and the difficulty rises gradually. Clear silhouettes, controls, tubing and supports provide the clues, while the answer review explains each item’s broad hospital purpose in plain language.

Your final percentage reflects only this entertainment challenge. Recognising equipment in photographs does not demonstrate clinical competence, safe operating knowledge or readiness to use any medical device.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Inspect each photograph and choose the one name that best identifies the hospital item shown.
Correctness stays hidden while you play, so compare the object’s shape, controls and attachments carefully.
Finish all ten pictures to reveal your Medical Equipment Score and complete answer review.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This quiz is not medical training, a clinical assessment or instruction for using healthcare equipment.

profiles.title: The Equipment Expert
profiles.copy: You recognised the defining details of almost every hospital item, including the specialist equipment. Very little in this equipment check could catch you out.

profiles.title: The Ward-Ready Spotter
profiles.copy: You identified hospital equipment with excellent accuracy and read the visual clues confidently. Only one or two specialist silhouettes kept the challenge interesting.

profiles.title: The Hospital Item Natural
profiles.copy: You recognised a strong majority of the equipment and separated several lookalike items correctly. Your visual hospital knowledge is in excellent shape.

profiles.title: The Clinical Kit Detective
profiles.copy: You found the purpose behind many familiar shapes while a few specialist devices stayed mysterious. The review will show the details that distinguish them.

profiles.title: The Equipment Explorer
profiles.copy: Half of the hospital collection felt familiar and half delivered a genuine surprise. That is a solid starting point for a fast equipment challenge.

profiles.title: The Medical Mystery Solver
profiles.copy: Several specialist items proved difficult, but every explanation turns a missed picture into a useful piece of general hospital knowledge.

insights.overview: Your equipment score at a glance

details.analysisTitle: How to read your equipment score
details.analysisCopy: This ten-picture result combines mobility aids, bedside supports, examination tools, monitoring devices and specialist equipment. Each correct identification moves the headline percentage by ten points.
details.roadmapIntro: Your score is the first signal. Continue through the report to see which equipment groups felt most familiar and review every missed item.
details.positionCopy: The entertainment challenge target is eight correct identifications out of ten. Your marker shows how close this attempt came.
details.measuredIntro: The selected photographs span five broad types of hospital equipment.

measuredAreas.title: Ward equipment
measuredAreas.copy: Recognising mobility aids and adjustable bedside supports used around hospital wards.

measuredAreas.title: Examination and monitoring
measuredAreas.copy: Identifying handheld assessment tools and machines that record important measurements.

measuredAreas.title: Specialist equipment
measuredAreas.copy: Spotting controlled-delivery and sterilisation devices by their distinctive chambers, screens and tubing.

details.tipsTitle: Three ways to identify hospital equipment
details.tipsIntro: Use these visual clues if you attempt the picture challenge again.

tips.title: Follow the attachments
tips.copy: Tubing, cuffs, leads and hanging supports often reveal what category of equipment you are viewing.

tips.title: Notice where it would sit
tips.copy: Wheels, rails, poles and tabletop bases help separate transport, bedside and examination equipment.

tips.title: Read the control surface
tips.copy: A chamber, pressure gauge, waveform screen or programmed display can distinguish specialist machines.

questions.question: Which familiar listening tool is shown?

image.alt: A Y-shaped listening device with earpieces, flexible tubing and a round chest piece

questions.explanation: A stethoscope carries body sounds through flexible tubing to the listener’s ears and is commonly used to hear heart and breathing sounds.

questions.question: Which mobility aid is shown in this photograph?

image.alt: A wheeled chair with large rear wheels, smaller front wheels, a seat and foot supports

questions.explanation: A wheelchair provides seated mobility using large rear wheels, smaller front casters and foot supports.

questions.question: What adjustable ward item is shown?

image.alt: An adjustable wheeled bed with side rails, mattress sections and a headboard

questions.explanation: A hospital bed has adjustable mattress sections, side rails and wheels to support patient comfort and ward care.

questions.question: Which bedside support is shown?

image.alt: A tall wheeled metal stand with hooks at the top for hanging fluid bags

questions.explanation: An IV pole is a tall mobile stand with hooks that hold fluid bags above the patient.

questions.question: Which monitoring item is pictured?

image.alt: An inflatable arm cuff connected by tubing to a pressure gauge

questions.explanation: A blood pressure cuff inflates around the upper arm and connects to a gauge or monitor for a blood pressure reading.

questions.question: Which patient-transport item is shown?

image.alt: A narrow flat patient platform mounted on a wheeled metal frame with side rails

questions.explanation: A stretcher is a narrow wheeled platform designed to move a patient between locations.

questions.question: Which examination tool is shown?

image.alt: A small handheld tool with a triangular rubber head and a slim handle

questions.explanation: A reflex hammer has a weighted rubber head and is used by trained clinicians when checking tendon reflex responses.

questions.question: Which monitoring device is shown?

image.alt: An electronic bedside display showing several waveforms and numerical readings

questions.explanation: A patient monitor displays several measurements and waveforms together so trained staff can observe changes over time.

questions.question: Which controlled-delivery device is shown?

image.alt: A compact electronic device with a display, control buttons and tubing passing through its front mechanism

questions.explanation: An infusion pump is a programmable device used by trained staff to deliver controlled amounts of fluid through connected tubing.

questions.question: Which overhead hospital light is shown?

image.alt: A large circular ceiling-mounted light with many bright individual lenses

questions.explanation: A surgical lamp uses a broad array of bright lenses to illuminate an operating area while reducing obstructive shadows.
